chapter_theme: Sivavakkiyar turns the reciters of Agamas back to what is already at home: the curd in the hanging pot, the body that is thrown out when it tips over, the kin who cannot follow at Death's call. Against these he sets the Lord found within, as the breath held near the heart, as the five letters laid over the limbs, as the letters A, U and M, and as the coiled power roused through the root channel; the hall of Tillai and the city of Arangan are read into the body.
structure_note: The run opens with reproach (1039 to 1046: scripture, the pot, wealth, kin and Death), passes through praise and the inner light (1047 to 1053), raises the body-and-life question (1054), and ends in a set of letter-verses on A U M and the five letters (1055 to 1063), several of them in cipher.

1039.reading: You recite Agamas that stand outside understanding and cannot grasp the one straight path, lost on the way; like someone who leaves the curd in the hanging pot and goes into the town to look for butter: how can one keep company with such men without understanding?
1039.nuance: The curd at home is the Lord within and the butter sought abroad is what scripture and pilgrimage promise; the verse does not say that, it leaves the image to do the work. அறிவிலே புறந்திருந்த may mean the Agamas stand outside understanding or that the reciters stand outside the understanding the Agamas hold.

1040.reading: You do not look, bones melting, with the two halls joined; you do not discern the one truth that stands as the hall of form; passing beyond the imagining that stands as the hall of the womb, can you be clear that this is the holy hall?
1040.nuance: அரங்கம் (hall, stage) comes four times, and the last, திருவரங்கம், is the name of Srirangam; the verse plays the shrine's name against halls within. Who the two of இருவர் அரங்கம் are is not said; tradition takes the pair as Siva and Shakti, or as the two breaths. The sense turns on this unresolved pun.

1041.reading: You stand in love and desire for the womb-pit, poor wretches and revelling sinners; setting yourselves right again and again by truth, know and know again the reddened five letters and yourselves, whom they dissolve.
1041.nuance: குருக்கிடுக்கும் is obscure: perhaps 'caught in a crevice' (குருக்கு) or something gurus set up. சிவந்த அஞ்செழுத்து, the red five letters, is read in tradition as the pancakshara seen as light in the body. உருக்கழிக்கும் may mean the letters dissolve your form, or that you must dissolve your own form; both readings keep the five letters as what undoes the self.

1042.reading: Being born on earth and talking past all dispute, countless crores of gods say 'mine' and 'yours'; but as the pupil sits in the eye while the eye is covered, it is by this one's eye that the countless crores of gods see.
1042.nuance: The image is the pupil (கண்மணி) in the eye: the seeing in every seer, itself unseen. வழக்கலாது உரைக்கவும் is unclear, 'speaking what cannot be argued' or 'speaking against custom'. 1085 returns to the Lord as the pupil of the eye.

1043.reading: When a clay pot tips over they set it upright and stack it; when a bronze pot tips over they treasure it as still needed; when our pot tips over they throw it out saying it stinks: what maya is this, Lord, that stands mixed into thought?
1043.nuance: The body is the third pot, and the comparison is in what people do with the fallen vessel, not in the vessel itself. எண்கலந்து, mixed into thought or reckoning, makes the maya a thing of the mind. The closing line returns in 1076.

1044.reading: Sinners who pile up the firewood of the great wealth you have made: you do not know that the body will be lit with that firewood and burn; children, wives and kin, all of these are maya; when Death comes and calls, can they come along?
1044.nuance: விறகு, firewood, does double work: the wood of the pyre and, as editors take it, the fuel of pride (கர்வம்); wealth builds the pyre on which the body is burned. The last line is a question, and the expected answer, no, is left to the hearer.

1045.reading: Where he came and joined with the Lady, becoming one and two in the town that gained youth, he wears bones and konrai and dances in the hall; if one recites the five letters, many sins depart.
1045.nuance: The first two lines are hard: ஒருவராகி இருவராகி (becoming one and two) fits Siva and Shakti, and இளமைபெற்ற ஊர் (the town made young) may be Tillai or the body renewed by yoga. The close is plain and, for Sivavakkiyar, orthodox: reciting the five letters removes sin.

1046.reading: While you live beside your mansions with cattle and calves, wealth, wife and children rejoicing, Death's messengers come running and strike all at once; you have seen the truth, the body lying there and the life slipped out, and still you do not take it in.
1046.nuance: உண்மை கண்டும் உணர்கிலீர்: the reproach is not that people have not seen death but that seeing it changes nothing. The verse separates seeing (காண்) from realising (உணர்).

1047.reading: Our Supreme, who set the flawless company of deeds, whom the singing gods remember as the dancing foot; Father who took up the dance in the hall of lasting red gold; blue-throated, death-throated, eternally auspicious one!
1047.nuance: A praise verse with no argument. பழுதிலாத கன்மகூட்டம் இட்ட is unclear: the Lord who set the faultless sum of deeds (karma) in place, or who gave a flawless body (காயம்) to the gods. காலகண்டன், throat of death, pairs with நீலகண்டன், the blue throat from the poison.

1048.reading: Like the ash that burned and rose in a forest with no forest left, in a heart that has reached knowledge nothing 'good' remains at all; if one gathers awareness in with the flawless light and holds it, Sivayam grows clear like honey welling in the comb.
1048.nuance: நல்லதேதும் இல்லையே can be read two ways: the jnani's heart is beyond good and evil, burnt clean like the forest; or no good remains to be sought there. The honey in the comb is the second image, a slow welling after the fire.

1049.reading: If you set apart and consider the open space that ran within you, drinking, and came flying, your mind becomes that; think within the light that melts and runs everywhere, and it becomes the good cause for you.
1049.nuance: பருகி ஓடி, 'drinking and running', suits the breath more than space, so வெளி may be the breath's open expanse or the inner sky; tradition reads both. நின்மனம் அதாகுமே, your mind becomes it, is the claim: the meditator takes the nature of what is contemplated.

1050.reading: Full one, who stands as light and comes as fruit, pure, and who recites the teaching that cannot be taught; running like a road and going through the foot of the sky, 'the first Lord is his own lord' has stood for endless time.
1050.nuance: The syntax does not resolve. விண்ணடி, the foot of the sky, is taken in tradition as the crown of the head, where the light passes out. ஆதிநாதன் தன் நாதன் may mean the first Lord is lord even of this light, or that the Lord is his own lord.

1051.reading: In the hall of Tillai, the mansion the Lord raised, the body that came by understanding was made of the five; when the sound of the instrument has sounded and gone, in the nine gates that slip open, one and a crore of ones sat within as one.
1051.nuance: Tillai (Chidambaram) is read as the body, and அஞ்சு as the five elements that compose it. கருவிநாதம் is the sound of an instrument; tradition takes it as the breath or the inner sound that ceases at death or in absorption. The last line, the one and the crore sitting as one, is the merging of soul and Lord, or of the many souls in the one.

1052.reading: If by love you can bring near and settle the breath that sits in the heart and runs pressing, you can see the devotees' temple within the eight directions that spread out; the dragonfly runs and runs: say it, Swami!
1052.nuance: The method is breath held still, and the means named is love (அன்பினால்), not force. தும்பி, the dragonfly, is a figure for the breath or the soul that darts; the last line's address is abrupt, perhaps a refrain carried in. The temple seen is within.

1053.reading: O breath that bowed and prostrated to Tillai; O maya of single enjoyment that stands beyond the limit; in the open space of the heaven-world beyond the limit, white and red became one and stood joined with truth.
1053.nuance: வெள்ளையும் சிவப்பும், white and red, is a coded pair: tradition reads the seed of father and mother, or Siva and Shakti, or moon and sun. Since it is the breath (வாயு) that bows at Tillai, Tillai is within the body. ஏகபோகம் returns in 1090.

1054.reading: Did the body take the life, or the life take the body? If the body took the life, tell me, what was its form? When the body with its life dies, the life does not die; forget the body as true, see and realise, and then speak knowledge.
1054.nuance: The verse argues: a body that took a life would already have had a form, so the life must come first; and since the life does not die with the body, the body is not the self (உடம்பு மெய் மறந்து). 1083 and 1109 return to the question.

1055.reading: With the letter A you made the seven worlds; with the letter U you took on form and stood; with the letter M the world was deluded; A and U and M together, Sivayam sat.
1055.nuance: The three letters of Om are given three acts: creation, embodiment and delusion, and the three together are the Lord. The verse does not match them to the usual gods or to the five acts; it leaves M, the closing hum, as the letter of maya.

1056.reading: Humans deluded by eating mantras: mantras are not what wells from forgetting; what a mantra is, is the breath that rises in its heat; for those who have eaten the mantra there is no death at all.
1056.nuance: The claim is that a mantra is breath, not a word, and that 'eating' it is drawing it in. மறத்தில் ஊறல் is unclear, 'welling from forgetting' or 'from valour'; மதத்தெழுந்த may be the breath rising in heat or in intoxication. The last line is the Siddhar promise of deathlessness through breath.

1057.reading: What shall I say of what has no grammar? Of the nature that passes beyond the words of the fine Tamil that is recited; as lightning gathers into lightning and becomes lightning, within me there is nothing but the Lord and I.
1057.nuance: The verse disclaims its own medium: Tamil poetry cannot say it. The lightning image, the many flashes that are one lightning, is reused in 1088 with the Lord subsiding within the self.

1058.reading: As the banyan gathers into the banyan seed and becomes the banyan, you have grown and reached enjoyment without any other seed; you do not consider the six-fold knowledge, men without understanding! Look at this within yourselves: it has become Parabrahman.
1058.nuance: ஆறுவித்தை is unexplained: six kinds of knowledge, the knowledge of the six (adharas), or the seed (வித்து) of the way (ஆறு). The banyan in the seed says that the whole is in the self; Parabrahman is a Vedantic word unusual in this corpus.

1059.reading: The mantra that rose from A, as akara and ukara: for those who know which letter it is, there is no rising into birth here; if one seats the mantra that rose from SA in the Supreme, A and U and M together sat as Sivayam.
1059.nuance: சவ்வுதித்த மந்திரம், the mantra risen from SA, is the five letters that begin with சி. தற்பரம் is the Supreme, and editors take it as a place in the yogic body, the centre between the brows; on that reading the verse is an instruction to fix the mantra there. The closing line repeats 1055.

1060.reading: With the two NAs as legs, the uttered MA as belly, the two SIs as shoulders, the excellent VA as mouth and the two YAs as eyes, standing pressed into straightness, the five letters Sivaya stood in right order.
1060.nuance: The five letters are laid over the body as a figure: the paired letters go to paired limbs. The layout differs in detail from Tirumular's (941), which puts MA at the navel and YA as the light above.

1061.reading: Within the moving wheel whose root is the two and the one, you lay coiled in three rings like a curled dog; the conch's sound that rose in contention went through the root channel and sat in the city of Arangan as Sivayam.
1061.nuance: The coiled sleeper in three rings is kundalini as tradition pictures it (three and a half coils); சுணங்கு, a dog, is the Siddhar's homely image for the serpent. இரண்டும் ஒன்றும், two and one, may be the three channels; அரங்கன் பட்டணம், the city of Arangan (Srirangam, Vishnu's), is read as the crown of the head. The verse is in cipher throughout.

1062.reading: As the turtle that moves in the sea climbs the shore, lays its eggs, and while it roams the sea again they take their form, so to think within the body of our light of the gem-hall that stays within the petal is truly the good truth.
1062.nuance: The image rests on the belief that the turtle's eggs on the shore hatch by the mother's thought from the sea: thought alone reaches and forms what is far. மடல், a petal, is the lotus of the heart; மணியரங்கம், the gem-hall, puns again on Arangam. 1070 makes the same point with the wasp's nest.

1063.reading: The letter uttered and risen in the three mandalas, in the pillar that stands striking against them, and in the mouth of the hanging serpent; the mantra the mother who bore and the father raised and spoke: within the one letter that appears there is nowhere else to speak.
1063.nuance: The three mandalas are traditionally the regions of sun, moon and fire in the body; the pillar is the spine or the central channel; the hanging serpent is kundalini or, on another reading, the uvula. The mother and father may be Shakti and Siva or one's parents. 1064 repeats the last line.

links.note: Both set curd at hand against a fool who goes elsewhere: Tirumular's ritualist eats bitter things while ghee, milk and curd stand by; Sivavakkiyar's reciter leaves the curd in the pot and searches the town for butter. In both the dairy at home is the knowledge already within.

Tirumular's seekers lose it in the sea and look in a pond, not knowing he has entered the body; Sivavakkiyar's reciters look in the town for what is in the hanging pot. Both say the search is misplaced, not that it is too weak.

The potter's pot against the body: Tirumular says people keep a broken pot's shards but not the broken body for a moment; Sivavakkiyar grades the pots, clay restacked, bronze treasured, the body thrown out as stinking.

Both run wife, kin and gathered wealth into the burning ground: Arunagiri's body falls like a broken pot and is left at the pyre; Sivavakkiyar's wealth is the very firewood that burns it, and the kin cannot follow Death's summons.

The Kural's life flies off like a bird leaving its shell; Sivavakkiyar's life slips out and the body lies there. Both make the parting sudden and the body the thing left behind; Sivavakkiyar adds that people have watched it and learned nothing.

Tirumular's knower has no impurity, no caste and 'no good to seek'; Sivavakkiyar's heart that has reached knowledge has 'nothing good' left in it, like a burnt forest. Both put the knower past the pursuit of good, though Sivavakkiyar's line also admits the darker reading that the fire leaves nothing.

Both make the body the Lord's shrine: Tirumular names heart as temple, flesh as shrine, mouth as tower gate and soul as the linga; Sivavakkiyar makes Tillai's hall the body built of the five, with the nine gates as its doors.

For both the temple within is seen by the breath: Tirumular's breath rising swiftly lights the dark temple like a gem lamp; Sivavakkiyar's breath settled near the heart lets one see the devotees' temple in the eight directions.

Tirumular says people cling to body after body without knowing the bond between body and life; Sivavakkiyar makes that bond a riddle, which took which, and answers that the life does not die with the body.

Both parcel the Lord's work out by letters: Tirumular's one, two and three letters make the world, the pair and the light, and 'the great letter' brings delusion; Sivavakkiyar gives A the worlds, U the form and M the world's delusion. In both a letter is charged with maya.

Both promise escape from death through breath: Tirumular's yogi who holds prana and apana together and stays still has no Yama; Sivavakkiyar's eater of the mantra, which he says is the rising breath, has no death.

Tirumular says chant சிவாயநம in the right way and no birth follows; Sivavakkiyar says those who merely 'eat' mantras are deluded, since a mantra is the breath and not the sound. He does not reject the five letters (1045, 1059), so this limits what chanting is, rather than contradicting it.

Lightning within lightning: in 1057 it shows that the Lord and the self are one flash, so Tamil cannot say it; in 1088 the lightning rises, spreads and subsides to show the Lord in the self subsiding into the self, which the eye cannot see as it cannot see itself.

The banyan and its seed: the Naladiyar's tiny seed grows a vast shade to show that a small virtue in worthy hands spreads wide; Sivavakkiyar's banyan is folded back into its seed to show that the whole is already within the self. The same tree, growing outward in one and inward in the other.

Both map the five letters onto the body. Tirumular puts NA at the feet, MA at the navel, SI and VA at the shoulders and YA as the light above; Sivavakkiyar puts NA at the two legs, MA at the belly, SI at the shoulders, VA at the mouth and YA at the two eyes. The scheme is shared, the placements differ at VA and YA.

Both describe the coiled serpent of three turns in the body as the thing to be worked: Tirumular's serpent of three coils with the yantra and the twelve finger-breadths keeps the body from perishing; Sivavakkiyar's sleeper of three rings is roused as sound through the root channel to the crown.

The two verses share the closing cry என்னமாயம் ஈசனே. 1043 asks it of what people do with the fallen body; 1076 of the body's growth from pollen and flower and the fall of the senses. Together they frame birth and death as one maya.

source_issues: 1041: குருக்கிடுக்கும் is unclear and may be corrupt.
1047: கன்மகூட்டம் is unclear; the line may intend காயம் (body) rather than கன்மம் (deed).
1058: ஆறுவித்தை is unexplained and may be a corruption of a technical term.
1060: அழுர்ந்து is not a standard form, perhaps for அழுந்து (pressed in).
